title: [Transform] implement retention policy to delete data from a transform

timeline.body:
add a retention policy to transform to delete data that is considered outdated as part of a transform checkpoint.

fixes #67916

todo:

- [x] documentation changes
- [x] support for added counters in `_cat/transforms/`
@elasticmachine update branch
run elasticsearch-ci/default-distro
Pinging @elastic/ml-core (:ml/Transform)
this is the renamed `TransformIndexerTests`, no changes done
I moved the former `TransformIndexerTests` to `TransformIndexerFailureHandlingTests`, so this is a new file.
Why are you parsing it twice?
Is there a specific reason why you are not using the `declareNamedObject` parser option?

reply.body: I wasn't aware of that, seems like this wasn't available when I implemented `sync`, will check it out.

timeline.body: this change is unnecessary. I am not sure ES server actions like this follow the same formatting yet.

reply.body: no, it isn't. The change here is the addition of `public`, which is necessary for testing and I think it is ok to make it `public`. Formatting is the result of line length overflow.

timeline.body: why not use `declareNamedObject`?
same as before, `declareNamedObject` should work

I think using a message supplier here would be good as serializing the entire DBQ and query unnecessarily might not be wise if debug isn't turned on. (not a HUGE deal now, but as these things get large...who knows).
Do we want to call `getStats().markEndDelete();` even on failures? I am not sure how the stats react here.

reply.body: I followed the design pattern of `AsyncTwoPhaseIndexer` - also w.r.t. naming etc. We have a similar situation for search and indexing, on a failure the global counters are _not_ incremented. Stats are fine, too: when `markStart{Indexing/Search/Delete}` is called a member variable gets set, if you call it twice, this member gets reset without incrementing the global counter.

timeline.body: a message supplier here and in the trace for consistency.

it might also be good to log if there were bulk failures. (debug level for the full messages). 

I think it is possible (even with retries turned off) where the bulk scroll response has errors in it but still returns an "OK".
Could you add the appropriate line for the added category below?

As long as it doesn't hit performance, I prefer using proper time-relates types (`java.time`) instead of performing calculations directly (like division by 1000000).
Could these types be used here?

reply.body:
I implemented it the same way as the others, see:
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/master/x-pack/plugin/core/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/core/indexing/IndexerJobStats.java#L172

I don't want to do it differently than the other places. I agree about using time instead of low-level types, I might change it in _all_ places as a follow up.

timeline.body: Since the formatter decided it fits in one line, could you remove `+` operators?

reply.body: :facepalm: I will look into making the formatter to not do this

timeline.body: Could `+` operators be removed completely here and in other examples?
IMO the method is generic enough that it could be called "refreshIndex", without mentioning "destination".

reply.body: good point, however I don't want to allow a generic refresh. It seems to be better to remove the refreshRequest parameter and hardcode the dest index.

timeline.body: Should it stay like this or is it some debug leftover?

```suggestion
 * All implementations of `rentention_policy` are converted to a {@link DeleteByQueryRequest}, which is then executed by the indexer.
```

```suggestion
 * All implementations of `retention_policy` are converted to a {@link DeleteByQueryRequest}, which is than executed by the indexer.
```
Could you clarify how is the checkpoint made "exposed" other than just being "indexed"?
Wouldn't this cause problems when other types of policies are added in subsequent versions?

reply.body:
You could add the accessors to `RetentionPolicyConfig` so that you don't have to do this casting.

Or `RetentionPolicyConfig` know everything about itself it could have a `toDeleteByQueryRequest` method

Yeah it would? I think thats the idea. If you add a new policy, you sure better make sure to write a request converter. 

Throwing here is a good pattern. It enforces case handling.

timeline.body:
Partial review, will finish in the afternoon.

I wish renaming the unit test base classes was a separate PR but no worries, I'll be able to go through it.

👍  from me.

I really like how nicely it falls into the indexer finish flow.
Is there any integration test added for the new functionality? I couldn't find it in this PR and I think it would be beneficial.
